previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with HCV-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and a history of TIPS placement, was admitted for altered mental status following a fall at home. He was found confused and lethargic, with no evidence of head injury on CT. His symptoms were attributed to hepatic encephalopathy, which improved with lactulose. Workup ruled out infection, including negative blood and urine cultures and a non-infected pleural effusion. He underwent a therapeutic thoracentesis for hepatic hydrothorax, which improved his breathing. His TIPS shunt remained patent but showed increased velocity, prompting need for follow-up. The right axillary vein thrombus was managed with subcutaneous heparin due to bleeding risk. He was discharged home in stable condition with clear mental status, instructions to continue lactulose and rifaximin, and plans for outpatient follow-up on liver function, TIPS patency, and anticoagulation.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  MRI of the Abdomen.

INDICATION:  Recurrent HCC, status post RFA to two lesions.  Evaluate after
treatment.

TECHNIQUE:  T1- and T2-weighted multiplanar images of the abdomen were
acquired in a 1.5 T magnet.
Intravenous contrast: 8 mL Gadavist.

COMPARISON:  Right upper quadrant ultrasound from ___.  CT of the
abdomen from ___.  CT interventional procedure from ___. 
MRI of the abdomen from ___.

FINDINGS: 

Lower Thorax: There is a small right pleural effusion as well as a right
basilar consolidation.  The consolidation is nonspecific, and most likely
represents atelectasis.  A component of infection cannot be completely
excluded.  The size of the effusion has decreased since the prior CT.  Within
the limitations of MRI, the left lung base is clear.  The base of the heart is
normal in size.  There is no pericardial effusion.  Post sternotomy changes
are noted.

Liver: The liver is shrunken and nodular, compatible with cirrhosis.  There is
no background hepatic steatosis.  The patient has undergone 5 TACE procedures
to the right lobe of the liver.  Additionally, since the prior MRI from ___, the patient has undergone an RFA of a lesion in segment ___, as
well as a lesion in segment 8.

In the region of the treated lesion in segment ___, there is a new 40 x 36 mm
treatment zone (1005 cm 1, 31).  This sits immediately adjacent to an old
treated lesion that is unchanged.  There is internal coagulation necrosis in
both the new treatment zone, as well as the adjacent treatment zone.  Along
the inferior aspect of the zone, there is a small amount of high signal on the
T2 weighted images (10, 15), which may represent evolving hematoma.  There is
no evidence of residual or recurrent disease.

In the region of the treated lesion in segment 8, there is a round
well-circumscribed 37 x 37 mm ablation zone (1501, 56).  There is internal
coagulation necrosis.  There is no evidence of enhancement within the lesion
to suggest residual or recurrent disease.  The previously seen enhancement is
no longer present.  Lateral to the treatment zone, there is a linear tract of
high signal on the T2 weighted images (10, 14 and 16).  Within this tract is
high signal on the T1 weighted images.  This is compatible with an area of
hemorrhage from the RFA probe.  In comparison to the CT from ___,
which was obtained five days after the treatment, this area of hemorrhage has
slightly decreased in size.

Other treatment zones in the right lobe of the liver are unchanged.  This
includes one in segment 6 that measures 41 x 20 mm (1501, 66), as well as a
second one in segment 6 which measures 35 x 24 mm (1501, 61).  There is no
evidence of residual or recurrent disease surrounding these treatment the
zones.

Several subcentimeter cysts or biliary hamartomas are unchanged.  There is no
arterially enhancing lesion that meets OPTN-5 criteria for hepatocellular
carcinoma.

There is mild narrowing at the take-off of the celiac artery, which is
unchanged from the prior exam.  The hepatic arterial anatomy is conventional. 
A TIPS is in all unchanged position.  Evaluation for patency is limited due to
metallic artifact.  The portal and hepatic veins are patent.  A recanalized
paraumbilical vein is noted.

Biliary: There is no intra or extrahepatic biliary duct dilation.  The
gallbladder is not distended.  There is no MRI evidence of cholecystitis. 
Multiple stones are identified.

Pancreas: The pancreatic parenchyma is normal in signal and enhances
homogeneously.  There is no duct dilation or solid mass.  In the head/uncinate
process of the pancreas, there is a 4 mm cystic lesion and a 7 mm cystic
lesion (10, 32).  Both are unchanged from prior exam, and most likely
represent side branch IPMNs.

Spleen: The spleen is enlarged, measuring 14.1 cm.  There are no focal
lesions.

Adrenal Glands: The bilateral adrenal glands are normal.

Kidneys: The kidneys are normal.  There are no worrisome renal lesions,
hydronephrosis, or perinephric abnormalities.  A 38 mm simple cyst is
unchanged in the right kidney.

Gastrointestinal Tract:  There is a small hiatal hernia.  The stomach and
small bowel are otherwise normal in course and caliber without evidence of an
obstruction.  The imaged portions of the large bowel are normal in caliber. 
There is mild wall edema in all the visualized loops of the small and large
bowel, likely due to third-spacing.  There is a large amount of ascites, which
is not significantly changed from the prior MRI.

Lymph Nodes: There are few prominent periportal lymph nodes, though none meet
size criteria for pathologic enlargement.  There is no retroperitoneal or
mesenteric lymphadenopathy.

Vasculature: The abdominal aorta is normal in caliber without evidence of an
aneurysm or significant atherosclerotic plaque.  There are extensive
esophageal, perigastric, and perisplenic varices.

Osseous and Soft Tissue Structures: There are no concerning osseous lesions. 
Mild degenerative changes are noted throughout the spine.  The soft tissues
are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Posttreatment changes in the right lobe of the liver, as described above. 
There is appropriate treatment response in the RF ablated lesions without
evidence of residual or recurrent disease.  No lesions meet OPTN-5 criteria
for HCC.
2.  Small amount of hemorrhage in the RF ablation tract in segment VIII,
decreased from the prior CT.
3.  Cirrhosis with evidence of portal hypertension, including splenomegaly,
varices, and large volume ascites.
4.  Cholelithiasis.
5.  Small right pleural effusion and right basilar consolidation.  The
consolidation is most likely atelectasis, though a component of infection
cannot be completely excluded.

There is moderate ascites. There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation.

The main portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow.
The TIPS is patent and demonstrates wall-to-wall flow.
Portal vein and intra-TIPS velocities are as follows:
Main portal vein: 19.4 cm/sec, previously 35 cm/sec

Distal TIPS: 231  cm/sec, previously 214 cm/sec

Flow within the left portal vein is towards the TIPS shunt. Flow within the

KIDNEYS:  Limited views of the kidneys demonstrate no hydronephrosis.  Note is
